mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the quarters with positive GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within the last month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances with joint increases in HOUST and RSAFS, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% per month, the combination of high interest rates and inflationary pressure reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in the last month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in real personal consumption expenditures over two consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months with negative RSAFS growth, or the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
